rows: 1.1 DIVERSITY IN THE LIVING WORLD

If you look around you will see a large variety of living organisms, be it potted plants, insects, birds, your pets or other animals and plants. There are also several organisms that you cannot see with your naked eye but they are all around you.
you look around will see large variety living organisms potted plants insects birds your pets other animals and there are also several that cannot with naked eye but they all diversity the world
1.2 TAXONOMIC CATEGORIES
Classification is not a single step process but involves hierarchy of steps in which each step represents a rank or category.
classification hierarchy rank category taxonomic categories living world
1.2.1 Species
Taxonomic studies consider a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities as a species.
taxonomic studies group individual organisms fundamental similarities species morphological differences
1.2.2 Genus
Genus comprises a group of related species which has more characters in common in comparison to species of other genera.
genus related species genera characters common
1.2.3 Family
Family has a group of related genera with fewer similarities than genus and species.
family related genera genus species vegetative reproductive features
1.2.4 Order
Order and higher taxonomic categories are identified based on aggregates of characters.
order higher taxonomic categories species genus families characters
1.2.5 Class
This category includes related orders.
class related orders primata mammalia carnivora monkey gorilla gibbon tiger cat dog
1.2.6 Phylum
Classes comprising animals such as fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals constitute Phylum.
phylum classes fishes amphibians reptiles birds mammals
1.2.7 Kingdom
All animals belonging to various phyla are assigned to Kingdom Animalia; Kingdom Plantae comprises plants from various divisions.
kingdom animalia plantae animals phyla plants divisions
2.1 KINGDOM MONERA
Bacteria are the sole members of the Kingdom Monera. They are the most abundant micro-organisms.
bacteria kingdom monera micro-organisms
2.1.1 Archaebacteria
These bacteria live in harsh habitats such as salty areas, hot springs and marshy areas.
bacteria archaebacteria halophiles thermoacidophiles methanogens cell wall harsh habitats
2.1.2 Eubacteria
There are thousands of different eubacteria or true bacteria.
eubacteria true bacteria rigid cell wall flagellum
2.2 KINGDOM PROTISTA
All single-celled eukaryotes are placed under Protista.
protista single-celled eukaryotes photosynthetic protistan
2.2.1 Chrysophytes
This group includes diatoms and golden algae (desmids).
chrysophytes diatoms golden algae desmids fresh water marine
2.2.2 Dinoflagellates
These organisms are mostly marine and photosynthetic.
dinoflagellates marine photosynthetic pigments
2.2.3 Euglenoids
Most are fresh-water organisms found in stagnant water and have a protein-rich pellicle.
euglenoids fresh water stagnant pellicle protein cell wall flexible
2.2.4 Slime Moulds
Slime moulds are saprophytic protists.
slime moulds saprophytic protists decaying twigs leaves organic material
2.2.5 Protozoans
All protozoans are heterotrophs and live as predators or parasites.
protozoans heterotrophs predators parasites animals
2.3 KINGDOM FUNGI
Fungi constitute a unique kingdom of heterotrophic organisms.
fungi heterotrophic morphology habitat
2.3.1 Phycomycetes
Members occur in aquatic habitats, damp places or as obligate parasites on plants.
phycomycetes aquatic decaying wood moist damp parasites mycelium aseptate coenocytic
2.3.2 Ascomycetes
Ascomycetes are commonly known as sac-fungi.
ascomycetes sac fungi penicillium yeast saccharomyces saprophytic decomposers parasitic coprophilous
2.3.3 Basidiomycetes
Common basidiomycetes include mushrooms, bracket fungi and puffballs.
basidiomycetes mushrooms bracket fungi puffballs rusts smuts parasites
2.3.4 Deuteromycetes
Deuteromycetes are commonly known as imperfect fungi.
deuteromycetes imperfect fungi asexual vegetative sexual forms
2.4 KINGDOM PLANTAE
Kingdom Plantae includes eukaryotic chlorophyll-containing organisms commonly called plants.
kingdom plantae eukaryotic chlorophyll plants insectivorous parasites heterotrophic
2.5 KINGDOM ANIMALIA
Kingdom Animalia includes heterotrophic multicellular eukaryotic organisms whose cells lack cell walls.
kingdom animalia heterotrophic eukaryotic multicellular cell walls plants food
2.6 VIRUSES, VIROIDS, PRIONS AND LICHENS
Viruses, viroids, prions and lichens are discussed outside Whittaker's five-kingdom groups.
viruses viroids prions lichens whittaker acellular organisms
3.1 ALGAE
Algae are chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic organisms.
algae chlorophyll thalloid autotrophic aquatic fresh water marine
3.1.1 Chlorophyceae
Chlorophyceae are commonly called green algae.
chlorophyceae green algae unicellular colonial filamentous
3.1.2 Phaeophyceae
Phaeophyceae or brown algae are found primarily in marine habitats.
phaeophyceae brown algae marine
3.1.3 Rhodophyceae
Rhodophyceae are commonly called red algae due to r-phycoerythrin.
rhodophyceae red algae r-phycoerythrin marine
3.2 BRYOPHYTES
Bryophytes include mosses and liverworts commonly growing in moist shaded areas.
bryophytes mosses liverworts moist shaded
3.2.1 Liverworts
Liverworts usually grow in moist, shady habitats.
liverworts streams marshy damp soil bark trees marchantia thalloid
3.2.2 Mosses
The predominant stage of a moss life cycle is the gametophyte.
mosses gametophyte protonema spore
3.3 PTERIDOPHYTES
Pteridophytes include horsetails and ferns.
pteridophytes horsetails ferns medicinal soil-binders
3.4 GYMNOSPERMS
Gymnosperms have ovules not enclosed by an ovary wall and exposed seeds.
gymnosperms naked seeds ovules ovary wall fertilisation
3.5 ANGIOSPERMS
In angiosperms, pollen grains and ovules develop in flowers and seeds are enclosed in fruits.
angiosperms flowering plants pollen grains ovules flowers seeds fruits
